in_sanskrit.name: वरद
in_sanskrit.meaning: blessing, boon, mercy, grace, benevolence, gift
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: वरद् (varad) is a Sanskrit word that means blessing, boon, mercy, grace, benevolence, and gift. It is derived from the Sanskrit root वृ (vṛ), which means 'to rain', and the suffix द (da), which means 'giver'. In Hindu mythology, Varad is also the name of a form of Vishnu, who is the giver of blessings and boons.

vedic_reference.note: Varad is a Sanskrit word and a name of Lord Vishnu in Hindu mythology. It is derived from the Sanskrit root वृ (vṛ), which means 'to rain', and the suffix द (da), which means 'giver'. In the Rigveda, Varad is mentioned as a name of Indra, the god of rain. However, in later Hindu texts, Varad becomes synonymous with Lord Vishnu, who is the giver of blessings and boons.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Varad" is deeply rooted in Hindu culture and has significant historical importance. It is a name given to deities who are known for their boundless grace, compassion, and blessings. The word "Varad" is derived from the Sanskrit root 'vara', which means 'boon'. The deity Varadaraja, a form of Lord Vishnu, is renowned for granting the deepest wishes and desires of his devotees. The name "Varad" signifies the ultimate power of bestowing blessings and mercy, a quality that is highly revered and valued in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Varad" holds great spiritual significance as it embodies the divine qualities of grace, compassion, and blessings. It reminds us of the ultimate reality that the divine is not an impersonal force but a loving, compassionate being who is ever-present and always eager to grant us his blessings. The name "Varad" inspires us to turn towards the divine when we are In need of help, guidance, or protection. It encourages us to have faith in the divine's ability to grant us the deepest longings of our heart and to trust that the divine's plan for us is always for our highest good. Ultimately, the name "Varad" serves as a reminder of the divine's infinite love and mercy for all of humanity.
